 With the Trump-Xi summit happening this week, which outcome do you think is most likely? 

 Click here to take the poll and don't forget to share your thoughts in the WSB comments section . 
 
 
 
 
 
 
    
 
 
 
    
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Risks mount: Google's Gemini is the latest to break out . Microsoft ( MSFT ) AI chief urges guardrails .

 AI oversight: Trump will form an "AI Force,"  saying the U.S. won't stifle the industry's growth.

 New deal: Greenland-linked stocks soar after the U.S. and Denmark reach security deal .
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 High stakes 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
It's a busy week for world leaders, with the United Nations General Assembly and the highly anticipated meeting on Thursday between U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping. Discussions at both events are expected to focus on Iran, trade, the Ukraine war and AI safety.

 On the agenda: Starting off, Trump will address the UN General Assembly Tuesday morning. "The president will highlight how he has and his ​administration have confronted complex problems head-on around the world," said Mike Waltz, U.S. ambassador to the UN. "He will touch on the importance of ensuring that Iran never has a ​nuclear weapon … and he'll talk about some of the U.S.' accomplishments over the past year." Trump will then meet with global leaders, including Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the UK's Andy Burnham, Japan's Sanae Takaichi and Venezuela's Delcy Rodriguez. He will also host a multilateral meeting with Arab leaders to discuss the Iran war. Notably, China's President Xi Jinping will skip the UN General Assembly. 

 Staying relevant: The UN General Assembly is being held at a time when the organization has struggled to stay relevant. "UN diplomacy aimed at halting wars and easing civilian suffering remains paralyzed, while funding cuts have weakened UN capacity ," think tank  International Crisis Group observed. Trump has slashed U.S. contributions to the UN, withdrew from several UN bodies and even questioned the point of the organization. This year's session is also important as UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres' term is ending and there's no clear frontrunner to replace him. "The UN's fortunes over the next 12 months will depend in no small part on who its members select as the next Secretary-General," International Crisis Group stated. "She or he will face considerable pressure to hit the ground running and deliver quick wins for an organization whose credibility has waned."

 China focus: Perhaps more consequential is Xi's state visit this week, given the U.S.-China trade truce that will ​expire in November. Markets will be watching for concrete action on tariffs, rare earths and AI .  While a breakdown could renew pressure on supply chains and raise uncertainty, Trump has largely adopted a warmer  tone toward Xi, raising hopes of a more positive summit. Ahead of the meeting, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent held talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York. Bessent said the talks helped lay the groundwork for Trump to advance U.S. economic interests. According to SA analyst Damir Tokic, China's  rare-earth export ban will be the summit's main focus. Beijing paused the ban late last year, with the suspension set to expire in November. Tokic  warned that if the suspension is not extended, it could trigger a major systemic event and a highly volatile reaction in the financial markets.
